subject: ss-cardiology
title: Ventricular arrhythmias and sudden cardiac death

steps.tx: The validated **Brugada criteria** algorithm differentiates ventricular tachycardia from supraventricular tachycardia with aberrancy in wide complex tachycardia through 4 sequential steps. The algorithm checks for absence of an RS complex in all precordial leads, an RS interval greater than 100 ms in any lead, classic **AV dissociation**, and lead-specific morphology criteria in V1 and V6.

steps.tx: The rapid single-lead **Vereckei aVR** algorithm evaluates wide complex tachycardia solely utilizing **lead aVR**. VT is diagnosed when any of 4 features are present: an initial dominant R wave, an initial r or q wave width greater than 40 ms, a notch on the descending limb of a negative QRS, or a ventricular-to-atrial initial-to-terminal activation velocity ratio of 1 or less.

steps.tx: Idiopathic **RVOT VT** is a benign triggered arrhythmia arising from delayed afterdepolarizations in the right ventricular outflow tract, mediated by cAMP and sensitive to adenosine. The 12-lead ECG demonstrates a left bundle branch block morphology accompanied by a tall, positive **inferior axis** with prominent upright R waves in leads II, III, and aVF.

right.title: Aortic cusp / LVOT VT
points: LBBB or RBBB with inferior axis

steps.tx: Idiopathic left ventricular intrafascicular tachycardia, known as **Belhassen VT**, arises from a reentrant circuit incorporating the posterior fascicle and adjacent purkinje fibres. The ECG displays right bundle branch block morphology with superior left axis deviation. This unique arrhythmia is refractory to adenosine but exhibits exquisite therapeutic responsiveness to intravenous **verapamil**.

steps.tx: In patients with ischemic heart disease, **Scar-related monomorphic VT** is sustained by stable macroreentry around dense collagenous myocardial infarction zones. Catheter ablation maps critical border-zone channels displaying abnormal electrograms with fractionated **late potentials**, allowing precise substrate modification and ablation during sinus rhythm without requiring prolonged arrhythmia induction.

steps.tx: **Electrical storm** is an acute cardiac emergency defined by 3 or more distinct episodes of sustained ventricular tachycardia or ventricular fibrillation requiring defibrillation within a 24-hour window. Management incorporates deep sedation, endotracheal intubation, intravenous beta-blockade, amiodarone infusions, left **stellate ganglion block**, and emergent catheter ablation to suppress severe adrenergic overdrive.

steps.tx: **Torsades de pointes** is a polymorphic ventricular tachycardia occurring in the setting of acquired or congenital QT prolongation, featuring characteristic twisting of QRS apices around the isoelectric line. Emergency pharmacotherapy requires an immediate intravenous **magnesium sulfate** bolus of 2 g, correction of serum hypokalemia, and temporary transvenous overdrive pacing to shorten the repolarisation interval.

right.title: Monomorphic VT
points: Normal or unchanged baseline QTc interval

steps.tx: An implantable cardioverter-defibrillator provides definitive mortality reduction in survivors of aborted sudden cardiac death. A **Secondary prevention ICD** is recommended for patients who have survived cardiac arrest due to VF or experienced sustained **hemodynamically unstable** ventricular tachycardia, provided the life-threatening arrhythmia did not occur within 48 hours of an acute transmural infarction or from an entirely reversible etiology.
